coachingPoints: ICE is a sideline coverage — never ICE a middle pick & roll
The on-ball defender must get his body to the ball handler's top hip early
The big stays deep and square, giving the guard time to recover
The weak-side low man is the safety net — he must be ready to rotate to the roller
If the ball handler rejects and goes middle anyway, the big must be ready to contain
commonMistakes: ICING a middle ball screen — the coverage has no sideline to use as a defender
The guard arriving late to the top hip — the ball handler turns the corner clean
The big stepping up too high — now there is no rim protection behind the ICE
The weak side falling asleep — the skip pass to the corner is wide open
description: ICE defense: force the ball handler down toward the baseline and trap him against the sideline on side pick & rolls.

diagram.title: ICE: X1 forces O1 down, X5 stays deep to contain

gameSituations: Side pick & rolls where you can use the sideline as an extra defender
Against a right-hand-dominant guard — ICE him to his weak hand
Late game when you want to keep the ball on one side of the floor
Against teams that run middle pick & roll poorly — force everything sideways

howTo.detail: Before the screen arrives, the on-ball defender gets his chest to the ball handler's top shoulder — the shoulder nearer the middle of the floor. His body, plus the screener, forms a wall that funnels the ball down.
howTo.title: Get to the top hip early

howTo.detail: The defender's stance and the sideline together deny the middle. The ball handler's only path is down toward the baseline, exactly where the defense wants him.
howTo.title: Deny middle, force baseline

howTo.detail: The screener's defender stays back and square — a soft drop — keeping his body between the ball handler and the rim as the ball is pushed down.
howTo.title: Big stays deep and square

howTo.detail: As the ball handler drives down, the big contains him while the on-ball defender recovers from behind. The ball is now trapped between two defenders and the sideline.
howTo.title: Contain against the sideline

howTo.detail: The weak-side defenders rotate: the low man is ready for the roller, the others sink to take away the skip pass. The ball is stuck on one side with limited options.
howTo.title: Weak side rotates to take away escapes

title: ICE Defense
whatIsIt: ICE is a side pick & roll coverage that forces the ball handler away from the screen and down toward the baseline. The on-ball defender jumps to the ball handler's top side before the screen arrives, using his body and the sideline as extra defenders to trap the ball on one side of the floor.

The name comes from 'icing' the screen — freezing it out so it never gets used. Instead of fighting through the pick, the defense simply refuses to let the ball handler use it, pushing him into a shrinking space along the sideline where help is waiting.
whyItMatters: ICE turns the sideline into a sixth defender and keeps the ball on one side of the floor, which simplifies every rotation behind it. It is the coverage of choice against dominant ball handlers on the wing — but it only works on side screens, and it demands discipline: one late step to the top hip and the whole thing collapses.
